data.verdict: F-2 is substantially delivered and the architecture claims hold up under adversarial checking. Three real gaps block a clean close: the status bar reports a capture round-trip as 'latency' where the plan mandates an explicit placeholder, the iOS tool dot is hardcoded instead of probed (the probe machinery already exists and is unit-tested), and Escape/close is unimplemented for the device picker (A11Y-4). Everything else flagged is either a human-gate judgement call or cosmetic.

findings.issue: The status bar will print a latency NUMBER where the plan mandates an explicit placeholder. ScreencapMirrorTransport sets latencyMs to the host-side capture round-trip on every frame, so TransportStats.latencyMs is never null during a session and StatsFormatter's placeholder branch is dead in production. A reader will take that number for the NFR-1 glass-to-glass latency it is not — which is precisely the honesty the NFR-1 waiver was granted on.
findings.description: ScreencapMirrorTransport.kt:95 reports captureMs as latencyMs; plan requires null + placeholder for the polling transport.
findings.evidence: data-device-impl/src/desktopMain/kotlin/data/device/impl/source/transport/ScreencapMirrorTransport.kt:95 `latencyMs = captureMs,` — unconditional. Contradicts plan.performanceBudget 'Status-bar content' -> "latency as '—'" and the NFR-1 row -> "the polling transport cannot even measure it end-to-end, so TransportStats.latencyMs is null and the status bar shows an explicit placeholder". The placeholder path at presentation-feature-mirror/.../core/stats/StatsFormatter.kt:38 (`stats.latencyMs?.let { "latency $it ms" } ?: latencyPlaceholder`) is therefore unreachable while streaming; only StatsFormatterTest exercises it.

findings.issue: AC-1 asks for a status dot reflecting DETECTED tool versions for BOTH platforms. The iOS dot is a hardcoded not-installed constant, never a probe. This is a gap, not an acceptable deferral, because the probe machinery already exists and is already unit-tested: ToolKind.Idb, probeCandidates' non-SDK branch, ToolResolver.readVersion's Idb case, installCommand and envHint are all shipped. Only a datasource member and one repository call are missing.
findings.description: iOS tool detection is a hardcoded constant although ToolResolver already supports ToolKind.Idb.

Capability that already exists and is tested: data-device-api/.../model/ToolKind.kt:21 `Idb("idb", null)`; data-device-impl/.../core/tool/ToolResolver.kt:91/110/116 (Idb version/install/env branches); data-device-api/src/commonTest/.../ToolProbeCandidatesTest.kt:93 `a tool that does not ship in the sdk skips the sdk roots`. The code comment at presentation-feature-mirror/.../source/mirror/MirrorContent.kt:212 ("iOS is probed so the user can see it is installed") is factually false today.

findings.issue: A11Y-4 ('Escape closes the picker only when a device is already selected') is not implemented in the UI at all. `Key.Escape` does not appear anywhere in the repository. MirrorIntent.ClosePicker has a reducer and two tests but no production dispatcher, and DevicePickerPanel ships no close affordance either — so re-opening the picker from the toolbar DeviceChip (AC-43) is a one-way door: the only way out is Enter, which starts a session.
findings.description: No Escape handler and no close affordance for the device picker; ClosePicker intent is test-only.

MirrorIntent.ClosePicker is declared at presentation-feature-mirror/.../MirrorContract.kt:206... (ClosePicker at MirrorContract.kt:169), handled at MirrorViewModel.kt:98, and dispatched only from MirrorViewModelSessionTest.kt:181 and :193.

findings.issue: HARDWARE GATE — ADJUDICATED: let F-2 close with the performance budget unverified, PROVIDED AF-1 is fixed first. The executor behaved correctly: no number was invented, CaptureFloorMs stays at an honest 100 ms, and a 5-step re-measurement harness is in the KDoc. NFR-1 was already waived at Stage 1 and re-flagged for pre-ship review, so the measurement is not a release gate for F-2 itself. But the waiver was granted on the premise that the UI stays honest about what it cannot measure — which AF-1 currently breaks. Fix AF-1 and the waiver stands on its own terms; leave AF-1 and F-2 ships a number that quietly contradicts it.

findings.issue: ADJUDICATED: the gap is real and cheap to close, so close it rather than waive it. ProcessRunner's timeout, destroyForcibly-in-finally, orphan registry and concurrent dual drain are the highest-risk code in the feature and the only new production class with ZERO automated coverage. None of it needs a phone: `/bin/sh -c 'sleep 5'` with timeoutMs = 100 asserts the timeout path and that the child is dead afterwards; `/bin/sh -c 'printf ... >&2; exit 3'` asserts the non-zero-exit and stderr-tail path; a large stdout writer asserts the no-deadlock drain. data-device-impl already has a desktopTest source set.

findings.issue: The plan's security prose overstates mechanism (2). DeviceCommand is NOT free-text-free: GetProp carries an unvalidated String that lands in `adb shell getprop <name>`, and adb re-joins shell arguments into a device-side sh command line — so a hostile name would be device-side injection, not an inert argv element. NFR-5's real-world guarantee survives only because GetProp is constructed nowhere in production code, which also makes it dead API surface. Either validate the property name (same treatment as DeviceId/AvdName) or delete the member.
findings.description: DeviceCommand.GetProp(name: String) is free text, contradicting the 'no free text' claim; also unused in production.
findings.evidence: data-device-api/.../model/DeviceCommand.kt:25 `public data class GetProp(public val name: String) : DeviceCommand`. Argv at data-device-api/.../parse/DeviceArgv.kt:63 `is DeviceCommand.GetProp -> listOf("shell", "getprop", name)`. `grep -rn "GetProp("` over the repo returns only the declaration and DeviceArgvTest.kt:27 and :73 — zero production construction sites. plan.security.dataHandling[0] mechanism (2) claims 'no vararg, no free text'.

findings.issue: ADJUDICATED: ACCEPT the vacuous satisfaction of T7-TAC3; require no change. The criterion's intent is that a reader can find out why a call is unbounded. There are genuinely zero withTimeoutOrNull sites in the domain layer because every child process is bounded inside ProcessRunner, and each use case that could plausibly want a deadline carries a comment saying why it has none. Adding a second redundant bound would make the failure mode WORSE — the KDoc explains that a domain-level withTimeoutOrNull can only express itself as null, which the UI cannot distinguish from a missing tool.

aggregateDiffFindings.issue: DeviceCommand.GetProp carries unvalidated free text into `adb shell getprop <name>`, which adb re-joins into a device-side sh command line. Contradicts the plan's 'no free text' claim; harmless today only because nothing in production constructs it. See AF-9.

Four production-unreachable artefacts: MirrorIntent.ClosePicker, MirrorIntent.StopMirroring, mirror_emulator_none, mirror_status_ready. Each has a reducer or a definition and a test, and no dispatcher or reader. Two of the four (ClosePicker, mirror_emulator_none) are symptoms of real gaps (AF-3, AF-6), not merely dead weight.
Two test-naming conventions in one feature: camelCase in the B4/B2 suites, backtick sentences in the B1 suites and in every pre-existing test. See AF-16.

No performance regression found, and the hot-path design is sound: single-flight by construction (the loop awaits the capture before issuing the next), overrun slots counted rather than smoothed (:79), PNG size read from the IHDR header per frame so rotation follows (:112), frame bytes passed by reference through MirrorFrameMapper rather than copied, and pixels bypass Orbit entirely via MirrorViewModel.frame so a 10 fps stream cannot cause 10 state copies a second. The only perf-relevant defect is reporting (AF-1), not throughput.

NFR-5 VERIFIED ADVERSARIALLY AND HOLDS. I looked for a raw-argv path, a public constructor and a String overload and found none. All five ProcessRunner entry points go through buildDeviceArgv/buildHostArgv (ToolResolver.kt:94, AdbHostSourceImpl.kt:28, EmulatorSourceImpl.kt:29 and :45, DeviceCommandExecutorImpl.kt:27); DeviceId and AvdName both have private constructors with validated factories and negative tests; DeviceCommandExecutor has one method with a non-defaultable DeviceId; ProcessBuilder appears in exactly one internal desktopMain file; `connect`, `-H` and `-P` appear in no command member. The one soft spot is that the DOMAIN seam is stringly typed (DeviceRepository.mirror(deviceId: String), bootEmulator(avdName: String)) — but both re-validate through DeviceId.of / AvdName.of at the data boundary (DeviceRepositoryImpl.kt:114 and :120) and reject rather than pass through, so the guarantee is not weakened, only enforced one layer lower than the prose implies.

SCOPE DISCIPLINE CLEAN. Nothing from F-3 (error cards), annotation, measure, payload, history or MCP appears in the diff. presentation-core-ui/.../organism/error/ErrorCard.kt is untouched and pre-existing. gradle/libs.versions.toml diff is 0 lines (independently confirmed). No TODO/FIXME/HACK, no println, no literal Color(0x or TextStyle( in added lines; two @Suppress("LongParameterList") on genuinely slot-heavy composables. Largest new file is 421 lines.
